item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-a9348eb37fb99833","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Ahead of the 2024 national election, Bangladesh authorities carried out mass arrests of opposition members; leaked police meeting minutes indicated a plan to secure convictions that would disqualify opposition members from contesting. The BNP estimated that half of its five million members faced politically motivated prosecution.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.3","2B.6","3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 pre-election conduct.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conduct to Bangladesh authorities and senior police officials during Sheikh Hasina's premiership.","limitations":["The leaked minutes and prosecution estimate are reported by Human Rights Watch rather than independently reproduced in the supplied text."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9348eb37fb99833","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The government replaced the Digital Security Act with the Cyber Security Act in September 2023, but the new law retained broad and abusive provisions used to criminalize expression; authorities also sentenced Odhikar leaders to two years in prison and refused a UN offer to establish a specialized mechanism for enforced-disappearance investigations.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 legal and institutional actions.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the legislation, prosecutions, and refusal of UN assistance to the government under Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["The supplied text reports allegations and assessments; it does not provide the full statutory text or judicial records."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9348eb37fb99833","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Journalists faced increasing attacks, self-censorship, demands to remove articles, and judicial targeting. After Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina called Prothom Alo an enemy of the Awami League, democracy, and the people, the newspaper's offices were vandalized.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 media conditions and a 2023 parliamentary speech.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the statement to Sheikh Hasina and other restrictions to government authorities.","limitations":["The report does not establish that Sheikh Hasina ordered the subsequent vandalism."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9348eb37fb99833","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Authorities retained broad powers under the Cyber Security Act to criminalize critics; labor organizer Shahidul Islam was beaten to death, labor-law protections remained inconsistent with ILO standards, and the government raised garment workers' minimum wage from US$75 to US$113 after protests, still below an estimated living wage.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","5B.8","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.7","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 law, labor violence, and wage policy.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the law and wage decision to the government; it does not attribute the killing directly to Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["The wage increase is a concrete favorable policy response, but the report gives no evidence of broader implementation or incidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9348eb37fb99833","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Women and girls had limited access to protection and justice; 51 percent of girls were reportedly married before age 18 and fewer than 1 percent of investigated rape cases led to conviction. Police subjected eight hijras to forced nudity and public presentation after arrest, while people with disabilities protesting for higher allowances were attacked and the allowance was not increased despite commitments.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","4B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.7","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns reported conditions and government conduct relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes police conduct and allowance policy to Bangladesh authorities; it does not establish personal direction by Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["Some statistics describe persistent conditions rather than changes occurring exclusively within 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a9348eb37fb99833","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Authorities imposed growing restrictions on Rohingya refugees, including barriers to education, livelihoods, movement, and assistance; failed to protect camps from armed-group violence; and pursued a pilot return project to Myanmar marked by coercion and deception. Donor shortfalls caused food-ration cuts.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 refugee policy and conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes restrictions, protection failures, and repatriation policy to Bangladesh authorities.","limitations":["The ration shortfall was partly caused by international donor underfunding, an external constraint."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95dde5815d081231","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In 2022-2023, authorities threatened and surveilled human-rights defenders and relatives of dissidents, denied renewal of Odhikar's registration, and pursued criminal cases against its leaders. Sheikh Hasina awarded two RAB officials sanctioned for human-rights abuses prestigious police medals; allegations also described secret detention, torture, and deaths in custody.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","8B.4","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source is primarily a 2023 report on 2022 events, with some conduct and institutional status continuing into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the medals to Sheikh Hasina and other actions to Bangladesh authorities.","limitations":["Some underlying abuses and administrative actions predate 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95dde5815d081231","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Authorities continued arrests under the Digital Security Act and ignored international calls to reform it; schools reopened in July after prolonged pandemic closures; the cabinet approved a draft amendment removing some ability to denigrate women's character in sexual-violence cases; refugees faced movement and education restrictions; and the government canceled a coal-plant project but planned an LNG replacement.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.5","3B.7","4B.6","4B.9","5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Mostly concerns 2022 conditions and decisions reported in a 2023 country report; limited direct fit to 2023-2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the legal, education, refugee, and energy decisions to Bangladesh authorities or the cabinet.","limitations":["Most dated events are from 2022, so period fit for 2023 is limited."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9aa2a9c15f7017a8","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"In the months before the January 2024 election, the AL rejected the BNP's demand for a neutral caretaker government. Between December 2022 and November 2023, ACLED recorded more than 420 BNP demonstrations, 43 percent of which became violent; police used live ammunition, at least five people were killed in clashes, thousands of BNP supporters were detained, and at least eight died in police custody after October 28.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.3","2B.6","3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.8","4B.9","7B.7","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 events, including December 2022-November 2023 trends.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the rejection of the caretaker demand to the Awami League government and the repression to police and security forces under Sheikh Hasina's government.","limitations":["ACLED records violence involving both opposition demonstrators and state forces; not all deaths are attributed solely to government action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-84ad4f9349877c72","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Freedom House assessed Bangladesh as Partly Free. It reported that the AL consolidated power through harassment of the BNP, critical media, and civil society; corruption controls were politicized; security forces acted with near impunity; the BNP boycotted the coming election and thousands of members were arrested; and the Cyber Security Act replaced the Digital Security Act without resolving concerns about suppression of online speech.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly summarizes 2023 political and institutional conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the consolidation and government actions to the ruling Awami League under Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["Freedom House is an external assessment and does not provide underlying case files for every claim."]},{"source_id":"SRC-84ad4f9349877c72","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The Election Commission was criticized for weak independence; some 2023 local elections showed improved performance because opposition and independent candidates won, but observer accreditation raised concerns about expertise and AL links. The BNP's political space narrowed after it adopted strikes and blockades; more than 20,000 members were reportedly imprisoned and at least eight died in custody. Women, minorities, and LGBT+ people remained underrepresented politically.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.7","4B.8","4B.9","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 electoral administration and political participation.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes election administration, arrests, and political restrictions to state institutions under the AL government.","limitations":["The report records both limited local-election improvements and broader national-level restrictions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-84ad4f9349877c72","start_unit":8,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Corruption safeguards and the Anti-Corruption Commission were weakened by political interference; media and NGOs faced restrictions; journalists were pressured; the CSA preserved repressive features; public political expression was constrained by fear; assembly rights were inconsistently upheld; labor organizers faced intimidation; and the judiciary and due process were politicized.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns conditions and institutional developments reported for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes politicized enforcement, legal restrictions, and institutional pressure to the AL government under Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["Some described institutional weaknesses are longstanding rather than newly created in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-84ad4f9349877c72","start_unit":13,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Rohingya refugees and other marginalized groups faced restricted access to services and security; camps experienced violence and dangerous displacement. Women faced discrimination and gender violence, garment conditions remained unsafe, and trafficking-law enforcement was inadequate, although the 2023 US assessment noted more investigations and prosecutions than in the prior period.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns conditions and policy implementation relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes refugee, labor, social-protection, and enforcement conditions to Bangladesh institutions; it also notes some improvement in trafficking investigations and prosecutions.","limitations":["Several conditions are structural and not uniquely attributable to decisions made during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9aa2a9c15f7017a8","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The AL's abolition of the caretaker-election system in 2011 was followed by continued AL rule; the 2018 election involved allegations of vote rigging and reprisals. In 2023, Hasina resisted calls to hold the 2024 election under a caretaker government, while opposition parties alleged misuse of state institutions to repress opponents and influence the election.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.3","2B.6","4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.8","4B.9","7B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Includes historical context and a direct 2023 decision relevant to the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes resistance to a caretaker government to Sheikh Hasina and the AL.","limitations":["The 2011 and 2018 events are context rather than 2023 events."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-ea0b8892a8e7f538","SRC-efc1a69d0cbe2fc8","SRC-757d7dba7b80f981","SRC-c931eb7900d90b8b","SRC-55df815c8a517d39","SRC-d4319de770cf6e5a","SRC-7270efafc72971b3"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents concern 2022, 2024, 2025, or 2026 rather than 2023-2023; facts from those documents were included only where they directly described 2023 conduct or provided clearly relevant period context.","The supplied documents contain substantial human-rights and electoral evidence but little or no direct evidence about nuclear risk, macroeconomic policy, social-service budgets, personal financial integrity, or formal effectiveness records."]}
